content: # Construct Hamiltonian policy-iteration paths for multi-action Markov decision processes This file contains the open problem on Construct Hamiltonian policy-iteration paths for multi-action Markov decision processes. --- ## 1. Construct Hamiltonian policy-iteration paths for multi-action Markov decision processes Source paper authors: Ritesh Goenka, Eashan Gupta, Sushil Khyalia, Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan ### 1. Problem Background Consider a finite discounted Markov decision process (MDP) $M=(S,A,T,R,\gamma)$ with finite state set $S$ and action set $A$, transition probabilities $T:S\times A\times S\to[0,1]$ (so $\sum_{s'\in S}T(s,a,s')=1$), reward function $R:S\times A\to\mathbb{R}$, and discount factor $\gamma\in[0,1)$. A (deterministic, stationary/Markovian) policy is a map $\pi:S\to A$. For a policy $\pi$, its value function $V^\pi:S\to\mathbb{R}$ is $$ V^\pi(s)=\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^t R(s_t,a_t)\Big],\quad s_0=s,\ a_t=\pi(s_t),\ s_{t+1}\sim T(s_t,a_t,\cdot). $$ For policies $\pi,\pi'$, write $\pi\prec\pi'$ if $V^\pi(s)\le V^{\pi'}(s)$ for all $s\in S$ and $V^\pi(s)0$; the policy improvement theorem guarantees $\pi\prec\pi'$. Define the policy-improvement directed acyclic graph (PI-DAG) of $M$ as the directed graph whose vertices are all policies $\pi:S\to A$, with a directed edge $\pi\to\pi'$ whenever $\pi'$ can be obtained from $\pi$ by one policy improvement step (switching any nonempty set of improving actions). A directed path in the PI-DAG corresponds to a possible trajectory of some policy-iteration (PI) algorithm on $M$. A Hamiltonian path in the PI-DAG is a directed path that visits every policy exactly once; for $|S|=n$ and $|A|=k$, this would have length $k^n$ (visiting all $k^n$ policies). ### 2. Open Problem **Question 1.1.** For integers $n\ge 1$ and $k\ge 3$, determine whether there exists a discounted MDP $M=(S,A,T,R,\gamma)$ with $|S|=n$ and $|A|=k$ whose PI-DAG contains a Hamiltonian directed path, i.e., a directed path that visits all $k^n$ deterministic stationary policies exactly once via successive policy-improvement steps. ### 3. Known Results The open problem asks whether for every $n\ge 1$ and $k\ge 3$ there exists a discounted MDP whose policy-improvement DAG (PI-DAG) contains a Hamiltonian directed path, i.e., a strictly improving sequence that visits all $k^n$ deterministic stationary policies exactly once. In the source paper, Goenka et al. explicitly resolve the $n=2$ case positively: Proposition 2 constructs, for each $k\ge 2$, a 2-state $k$-action discounted MDP together with a policy-iteration switching rule whose trajectory visits all $k^2$ policies, giving a Hamiltonian PI-DAG path in that special case. For $n\ge 3$ and $k\ge 3$, the existence of Hamiltonian PI-DAG paths remains open in the material provided. The source paper emphasizes that known lower bounds for multi-action MDPs are far from $k^n$: the best cited lower bound for $k\ge 3$ is $\Omega(k^{n/2})$ iterations (from earlier work), and it even arises from deterministic MDP constructions, suggesting that substantially stronger lower-bound constructions are needed in the stochastic setting. The forward-citing work titled “An improved lower bound on the length of locally-improving policy sequences in MDPs with large action sets” indicates progress on extending these lower bounds when $k$ is large, but without its explicit bound it is unclear whether it approaches the Hamiltonian target $k^n$ or remains exponentially smaller. Overall, the state of the art is: Hamiltonian PI-DAG paths are known to exist for $n=2$ and all $k$, while for $n\ge 3$, $k\ge 3$ the main gap is constructing near-Hamiltonian (or Hamiltonian) monotone policy sequences under local improvement constraints. Promising directions include extending the 2-state Hamiltonian construction to 3 states (as suggested by the source paper), and leveraging large-action-set lower-bound techniques to engineer PI-DAG paths that systematically enumerate policies while maintaining strict improvement at each step. #### 3.1 Upstream solution and partial-progress records - [Partial progress #149 (PDF)](https://pranav-nuti.github.io/open-problems-in-or/data/llm_math_export/solution_progress/W4409316647_p0/partial_progress/149.pdf) ### 4.
